state.context: Target behavior is P8 native stdin collection with a user-supplied integer byte budget, immutable buffers, strict UTF-8 strings, io::limit_exceeded(int limit) and io::read_failed(str operation). The document neither caps max_bytes nor defines a negative argument. Arbitrary-size Can integers differ from finite native allocation limits. There is no backwards-compatibility requirement or runtime fallback. Before any narrowing, track size as bigint; do not keep data beyond the requested allowance, and cancel excess input while observing cleanup failures. Environment names satisfy [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]* and values come from the startup caller snapshot. Optional lookup distinguishes absence; required lookup reports http::credentials_missing when missing; an existing empty value remains present. Authentication separately refuses empty bearer secrets. Deterministic fixtures cannot read ambient state.

policy.instructions: Which read design follows the available specification most closely while avoiding an invented resource bound?

criteria.bounded: Use limit_exceeded for negative arguments and accept zero or larger bigint limits. Check each incoming chunk against remaining capacity, leaving unforeseen allocation exceptions as standard failures.
criteria.cap: Set an additional 64 MiB ceiling and classify every argument over it as limit_exceeded.
criteria.eager: Let the native API accumulate the entire input, then apply the caller size comparison.
